{{short description|Every nonzero proper ideal in the ring of integers of a number field factorizes uniquely}}
In [[number theory]], the '''fundamental theorem of ideal theory in number fields''' states that every nonzero [[proper ideal]] in the [[ring of integers]] of a [[number field]] admits unique [[factorization]] into a product of nonzero [[prime ideal]]s. In other words, every ring of integers of a number field is a [[Dedekind domain]].
